correctness.rationale: Exact exposed-edge obstruction yields c_V>=1 for every nondegenerate polygon. For a Minkowski center with -P subset sP, the copies H_v=(v+sP)/(1+s) each contain origin and jointly cover each edge since s/(1+s)>=1/2; convexity extends to the whole polygon, giving c_V<=s. Rotation averaging shows center 0 minimizes s on a regular polygon, and the opposite vertex radial intersection plus central nonmembership proves odd-n lower equality. No finite sampling or numerical computation is used. The classical s<=2 bound is standard.

value.rationale: The universal shape-sensitive affine invariant c_V<=s is stronger than the known planar dimension-only c_V<=2 whenever s<2 and applies to every polygon, with exact extremal infinite family where odd regular n have nontrivial sec(pi/n) factor. It quantifies a natural finite convexification problem and supplies exact sharp covering/noncoverage mechanisms rather than an arbitrary example.
